_comment: find_01RtSp6b2GvNCj76v7dhrLmg (high, CWE-799): a vendored allowlist of Google-announced address space that is NOT also announced for Google Cloud customer workloads (GCE/Cloud Run/GKE -- cloud.json). This is the egress Firebase Hosting's own serving layer uses when it rewrites /api/** to our Cloud Run service; Cloud Run's own ingress always appends the TRUE TCP peer it saw as the last X-Forwarded-For entry (never client-supplied), so if that peer is in this list, the request came in through a Google-operated hop (Firebase Hosting) and the real end-user IP is the entry before it. IMPORTANT, found the hard way (2026-11-07): goog.json (Google's full announced network, 132 IPv4 prefixes) is NOT disjoint from cloud.json (the customer-facing range, 1056 IPv4 prefixes) -- EVERY SINGLE cloud.json prefix falls inside some broad goog.json supernet (e.g. 34.64.0.0/10 covers both Google's own infra AND GCE customer addresses). Vendoring goog.json wholesale would have let an attacker who rents their own GCE VM or Cloud Run service get treated as a 'trusted hop' on the direct *.run.app path, re-opening the exact spoofing vulnerability this fix exists to close -- the earlier, attacker-forged XFF entry before a rented-GCP address would then be read as 'the real client'. This file is therefore NOT goog.json: it is goog.json's prefixes MINUS every one that overlaps ANY cloud.json prefix (79/132 IPv4, 15/16 IPv6 survive). 66.249.64.0/19 (the real lingoleap-staging.web.app egress Cloud Run logged as httpRequest.remoteIp=66.249.82.130 for a probe request, 2026-11-07, verified via `gcloud logging read`) is in this safe set. Refresh: re-run this same goog.json-minus-cloud.json computation against freshly fetched https://www.gstatic.com/ipranges/goog.json and https://www.gstatic.com/ipranges/cloud.json, diff before committing -- a reviewed change, same discipline as firebase-tools' pin in .github/firebase-cli, never a runtime fetch.
method: goog.json prefixes with zero CIDR overlap against any cloud.json prefix
